name: get_change_item
description: One change item with everything upstream says about it: the upstream change (title, detail text, subjects, references) or compatibility change, the upstream evidence records (URI, locator, verbatim excerpt), the upstream source artifacts (read them with read_artifact), migration notes, the release- and environment-scope rendered changes correlated to it, and the deterministic join's findings for it. Start every item here: for a controller-behaviour item the upstream text is where the setting that restores the old behaviour is named. Required before you explain an item or close it as explains / examined-no-concern.

name: get_dossier
description: The dossier of a change item: the change and its upstream text, the settings that decide it with their effective state on every exposed object (explicit / inherited-default / unknown, and where), correlated rendered changes, relevant unchanged configuration, attached knowledge facts, validations already run, relations, and the evidence gaps (missing / partial / contradictory). Your session already starts from its own item's dossier; use this for another item.

name: list_renders
description: Every render pair of the investigation: scope (environment = rendered with this environment's own configuration; release = chart defaults), target, status (only ok is a complete render; partial/unavailable are evidence gaps, never 'no change'), reason, number of rendered changes by class, and how many are uncorrelated (no change item explains them).

name: query_diff
description: Filter the rendered changes (the semantic before/after diff of the renders). Every set field must match; list fields match any element. Results come in a fixed order, at most `limit` per page; pass the returned `next` as `after` to continue. Unknown targets, change items, classes or cursors are rejected rather than answered with an empty page.

target.description: render target as list_renders names it

changeItem.description: only changes correlated to this change item

uncorrelated.description: only changes no change item explains

classes.description: render change classes, e.g. field-changed, container-arg-added, image-changed, rbac-permission-removed

pathPrefix.description: field path prefix inside the object

after.description: continuation cursor: the `next` of the previous page

name: get_rendered_object
description: One rendered object, or one field of it, from the from or the to render of a render pair, as YAML (secret values redacted). found=false means the object or field is absent on that side (a fact, not an error). The result names the render artifact: cite it with {artifact, locator: <object and path>, quote: <text from the YAML>}.

path.description: field path inside the object, e.g. spec.template.spec.containers[name=controller].args; empty = the whole object

name: search_manifest
description: Search the investigation's artifact manifest (upstream documents, environment files, renders, diffs, environment facts). `terms` must each match a tag, the path or the kind of an artifact; `grep`, an RE2 pattern, returns matching lines (bounded). Artifacts with secrets are searched in redacted form.

changeItem.description: only artifacts related to this change item

grep.description: RE2 pattern matched line by line

name: read_artifact
description: Read a window of an artifact's text: lines fromLine..toLine (1-based, inclusive; at most 400 lines / 64 KiB per call), or the node at yamlPath (dot path with [n] indices; a leading [n] selects the n-th YAML document, 0-based). Every byte returned counts against your read budget: read windows, not whole files.

name: expand_graph
description: The neighbourhood of a node of the relationship graph (secondary context: consumers a render cannot show). Edges point in the direction impact propagates: from the provider to the consumer. Status established = from evidence; inferred/missing = unresolved.

name: list_paths
description: Impact paths of the bounded traversal from each change item's exposure roots (the objects of its correlated environment rendered changes, then the join's matches).

unresolved.description: only paths with an inferred or missing edge

name: request_evidence
description: Ask for evidence the investigation does not have: an upstream artifact (a linked PR, a file at a tag), a change source whose status is not ok, an environment input that was not supplied. The request is recorded for the next collection round; nothing is fetched during this session. Live-cluster reads are disabled.

target.description: URL, change source kind, environment path or GVK

name: request_validation
description: Ask a deterministic validator to test a change item against environment subjects now. Kinds: override-inspection (does an explicit environment setting pin the old behaviour?), render-diff (does the item's effect reach these rendered objects?), schema-compat, static-reference, runtime. The validator, not you, produces the result (pass / fail / error / not-run); a validator that cannot decide never passes. Name subjects the way the evidence names them (a values key, a flag, an object); the resolution is returned with the result. To have a concern or mitigation claim answered, record the assertion first, then name it in `answers` (assertions recorded with this request's `hypothesis` are linked too).

subjects.description: what to check, each one of: graph node id (gn-…) or key (<group>/<version>/<kind>/<namespace>/<name>), a rendered change id (rc-…), an environment file (art-… or its path), an object reference Kind/name or Kind/namespace/name, a Helm values key (controller.replicaCount or values:controller.replicaCount), or a setting as it appears in a complete environment render (a container flag, annotation key, environment variable or config key). Each is resolved deterministically to graph nodes; the result says how.

paths.description: impact path ids of this change item

inputs.description: artifact ids you suggest the validator reads

answers.description: ids (asr-…) of your raises-concern / claims-mitigation assertions about this change item that this validation is meant to answer. A link is made only when the validation covers everything the assertion names (its subjects, impact paths and rendered changes; an assertion naming none needs an item-wide request, with no subjects, paths or rendered changes). The result says which links were made.

name: record_hypothesis
description: Record a testable statement about a change item, with at least one citation. Every citation is checked: the artifact must exist and the quote must occur verbatim in its bytes (whitespace-insensitive). Optionally, `mitigation` states the hypothesis as a proposed release-level rule in the fact grammar: the subject, how it changed, which objects are exposed (applicability), the consequence, and the release bounds; plus the environment basis (verified claim ids, validation ids or object references showing this environment meets the rule's conditions) and the verification you request. It is checked when recorded (complete and decidable grammar, the subject occurs in the bundle and belongs to the product, the bounds parse and lie within this upgrade, every basis reference resolves, at least one citation is upstream text); a malformed one is not stored and the result says why. A mitigation is a proposal for independent verification: it never clears anything by itself.

subjects.description: what to check, each one of: graph node id (gn-…) or key (<group>/<version>/<kind>/<namespace>/<name>), a rendered change id (rc-…), an environment file (art-… or its path), an object reference Kind/name or Kind/namespace/name, a Helm values key (controller.replicaCount or values:controller.replicaCount), or a setting as it appears in a complete environment render (a container flag, annotation key, environment variable or config key). Each is resolved deterministically to graph nodes; the result says how.

subject.description: {family, product, group?, version?, kind?, path?, name?, component?}; families: crd-field (group, kind, path), helm-value (path), cli-flag (name), env-var (name), feature-gate (name), config-key (path), gvk (version, kind), image (name), …

change.description: {type, before?, after?}; types: default-changed (before and after required, JSON-encoded), behavior-changed, removed, renamed, value-changed, …

exposure.description: a condition of the fact grammar: {op, of?, group?, version?, kind?, name?, path?, component?, state?, values?, pattern?, separator?, range?}. Combinators all/any/not; `resource` (kind, group?) scopes `field` (path, state unset|set|equals|not-equals|matches|has-token|has-token-key) to one object of that kind; environment-wide leaves values-key, cli-flag, env-var, feature-gate, gvk-in-use, image-in-use, product-version, cluster-version. equals/not-equals values are JSON-encoded ("\"Retain\""). No `undecidable` leaf: a rule must be decidable on an environment.

overlap.description: a condition of the fact grammar: {op, of?, group?, version?, kind?, name?, path?, component?, state?, values?, pattern?, separator?, range?}. Combinators all/any/not; `resource` (kind, group?) scopes `field` (path, state unset|set|equals|not-equals|matches|has-token|has-token-key) to one object of that kind; environment-wide leaves values-key, cli-flag, env-var, feature-gate, gvk-in-use, image-in-use, product-version, cluster-version. equals/not-equals values are JSON-encoded ("\"Retain\""). No `undecidable` leaf: a rule must be decidable on an environment.

consequence.description: {kind, exposedClass, statement?}; kind behavior-change → exposedClass review-required; setting-ignored / workload-failure / resource-rejected / … → action-required (statement required); none → informational

statement.description: the rule in one plain sentence

release.description: from = the last version with the old behaviour (exclusive), to = the first version with the new one (inclusive); semver, within this upgrade

environmentBasis.description: verified claim ids (clm-…), validation ids (vr-…) or object references (Kind/namespace/name, node ids) showing this environment meets the rule's conditions

requestedVerification.description: what an independent check must show to confirm the rule (both with and without the condition)

name: record_assertion
description: Record a claim about a change item with at least one checked citation. raises-concern = a plausible impact (blocks a not-affected conclusion until a passing validation answers it); explains = reasoning attached to the finding; claims-mitigation = you believe something mitigates the change (it stays an unvalidated assumption until a validation establishes it). A proposedEdge adds an inferred relationship (never established). An explains assertion is accepted only after get_change_item on its item and with at least one citation no other item's records share. A raises-concern counts as an item concern only for this session's item and only when it cites an artifact you retrieved in this session (read_artifact, get_rendered_object, grep lines of search_manifest, the item's sources via get_change_item, the renders behind query_diff results); otherwise it is recorded as an investigation-level note.

subjects.description: what to check, each one of: graph node id (gn-…) or key (<group>/<version>/<kind>/<namespace>/<name>), a rendered change id (rc-…), an environment file (art-… or its path), an object reference Kind/name or Kind/namespace/name, a Helm values key (controller.replicaCount or values:controller.replicaCount), or a setting as it appears in a complete environment render (a container flag, annotation key, environment variable or config key). Each is resolved deterministically to graph nodes; the result says how.

from.description: provider: node id, node key, or <node kind>:<key> for a node not in the graph

noValidationReason.description: for a raises-concern: why you are not requesting a validation (required for a concern on a controller-behaviour/unknown item unless you made a request_validation for the item in this session)

claims.description: ids (clm-…) of verified setting claims (record_claim) this rests on

name: submit_findings
description: End this session by closing THIS session's item with exactly one entry and a disposition: raises-concern, claims-mitigation, explains, examined-no-concern (cite what you inspected; not a mitigation, never lowers a class) or not-examined (the summary states why). Every disposition except not-examined needs at least one checked citation. Depth rules (checked here): explains / examined-no-concern need get_change_item on the item in this investigation and at least one citation not shared with another item; a raises-concern on a controller-behaviour/unknown item needs a request_validation for the item or a noValidationReason; a raises-concern must cite at least one artifact you retrieved for the item in this session, otherwise it is recorded as an investigation-level note, not an item concern. Accepted once even after the session budget is spent. After submitting, stop. State facts about what the environment sets with record_claim first and name them in `claims`; the summary itself is recorded as unverified AI prose. Every entry except not-examined carries `verdict`: your own provisional assessment of whether the change breaks THIS environment. It is recorded beside the policy's classification and measured against known outcomes; it never sets or lowers a class, and you may conclude not-affected where the policy cannot. Its citations and verified facts are checked one by one; whatever does not resolve is dropped and counted.

summary.description: closing summary; for not-examined, the reason

citations.description: at least one for every disposition except not-examined

noValidationReason.description: for a raises-concern: why you are not requesting a validation (required for a concern on a controller-behaviour/unknown item unless you made a request_validation for the item in this session)

claims.description: ids (clm-…) of verified setting claims (record_claim) this rests on

mechanism.description: the breaking mechanism: what changed and what it would break

environmentReasoning.description: how this environment consumes the behaviour, whether it exercises it, whether its effective configuration preserves the old behaviour, what the renders establish, which consumers could be affected

verifiedFacts.description: ids of verified claims (clm-…) and validation records (vr-…) the verdict rests on

mitigations.description: hypothesis ids (hyp-…) of mitigations you proposed

wouldOverturn.description: the evidence that would overturn this verdict

name: record_claim
description: State a fact about the environment in structured form, so it is checked instead of left as prose: setting S is absent / present / has value V in input X. The tool layer verifies it deterministically against the bundle's artifacts before recording it: a dotted key path (a.b.c) is looked up as a YAML path, and its last key is searched anywhere; a token (a flag such as --x, an annotation key, an environment variable) is searched as a whole word. `absent` is verified only when the setting occurs nowhere in the input in any of these forms. A claim that does not hold is rejected with the contradicting line. Use it for every statement about what the environment sets or does not set; cite the claim id in assertions and closing summaries (`claims`).

changeItem.description: the change item the claim is about (optional)

setting.description: dotted key path (controller.metrics.enabled) or a token (--enable-x, an annotation key, an env var name)

input.description: an environment file or environment render (artifact id or path), or "environment-files" for every environment file

value.description: kind value: the expected value, as a JSON or YAML scalar
